title: Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Has Died
author: La Jornada Editorial Staff
content:
_This article by La Jornada Editorial Staff originally appeared in the[October
28, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/28/politica/version-del-
fallecimiento-de-cuauhtemoc-cardenas), Mexico's premier left wing daily
newspaper._

Engineer Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas, **historic leader of the Mexican left** , has
died at the age of **92**.

The body of Engineer Cárdenas will lie in state tomorrow, **October 29,
between 10:00 and 16:00 at the Panteón Francés de Legaria** , where his wife
Celeste Batel, who died on October 19, 2021, also rests.

Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas was born on May 1, 1934. He was a presidential candidate
three times, in 1988, 1994 and 2000. He was the first head of government of
the Federal District chosen by popular vote, in 1997.

The son of former President of Mexico (1934-1940) General Lázaro Cárdenas del
Río, considered one of the best presidents the country has had, he obtained
his degree in civil engineering from UNAM's National School of Engineering in
1955.

In 1954 he began his membership in the Institutional Revolutionary Party
(PRI). His first participation was in the National Liberation Movement (MLN),
1961-1964, which within the PRI meant the ability to bring together young
people with concerns and channel proposals from groups far from power, and in
which figures such as Heberto Castillo, Enrique González Pedrero, Octavio Paz,
César Buenrostro, Clementina Batalla de Bassols, Manuel Marcué Pardiñas and
many other nationalists and leftists took part, inside and outside that party.

In 1974, with Jesús Reyes Heroles as president of the PRI and Luis Echeverría
President of the Republic, Cárdenas campaigned as a pre-candidate for governor
of Michoacán, but the candidate was Carlos Torres Manzo, which provoked a
public protest by the Engineer over the imposition.

He took part in José López Portillo's pre-campaign for the presidency in 1975.
He then had the candidacy for senator for Michoacán, and the Communist Party
candidate Manuel Pérez Adame withdrew his candidacy and supported Cárdenas. In
1980 he won the election and became **governor of Michoacán** for the PRI, a
term that ended in 1986.

In 1987, together with figures such as Ifigenia Martínez, Porfirio Muñoz Ledo,
César Buenrostro and Rodolfo González Guevara, they formed the **Democratic
Current of the PRI** , seeking the party's internal democratization, against
the designation of candidates by the sitting President of the Republic.

## Leaves the PRI in 1987

He left the PRI after considering that it had strayed from the principles that
gave rise to it in the Mexican Revolution and that the imposition by the
President of the Republic in the naming of who would be the presidential
candidate should not be accepted.

For more than a year he gathered supporters for that democratic cause, and on
October 14, 1987, the leader of the Authentic Party of the Mexican Revolution,
Carlos Cantú Rosas, nominated Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas as its candidate for the
Presidency of the Republic. Then the Popular Socialist Party and the Cardenist
Front for National Reconstruction Party joined, to form the **National
Democratic Front (FDN)** , with other small groups such as the Social
Democratic Party, the Mexican Green Party and later the Movement for
Socialism, which was made up of splinters from the Unified Socialist Party of
Mexico, the Mexican Workers' Party and the Revolutionary Workers' Party.

![Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas at a PRD rally in the Zócalo,
1989](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/02-cardenas-prd-
zocalo-1989.jpg)PRD rally with Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas in the Zócalo to announce
its birth as a party, May 5, 1989. Photo: Luis Humberto González / La Jornada

## Founder of the PRD

He then launched himself as presidential candidate of the so-called National
Democratic Front in 1988, while the PRI nominated Carlos Salinas de Gortari.
On July 6, the day of the presidential elections, in the face of **the famous
crash of the system** , Cárdenas, Manuel J. Clouthier (PAN candidate) and
Rosario Ibarra de Piedra (of the PRT) set aside their differences and went to
protest before the Secretariat of Governance.

![Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas, Andrés Manuel López Obrador and Heberto Castillo raise
their hands, 1989](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/03-cardenas-lopez-obrador-1989.jpg)October 21, 1989.
At the end of the event: Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas, Andrés Manuel López Obrador,
Navarrete, Castillo M., Heberto Castillo. Photo: Francisco Mata / La Jornada

The trends favored Cárdenas, who declared himself the winner with a trend of
**42 percent, to 36 for Salinas** , with 50 percent of polling stations
counted. Then the protests over the alleged electoral fraud began, the mass
rallies were repeated across the country, and many were waiting for Cárdenas's
call to defend the vote at the ballot boxes, but it did not happen. His
collaborators said that, had it happened, a civil war could have been
unleashed.

After the 1988 election, and with the **electoral fraud that brought Carlos
Salinas de Gortari to the presidency** consummated, he founded a political
party to continue his movement, now with an open rejection of neoliberalism
and in defense of social policies in favor of the lower classes and vulnerable
sectors, as well as government support for culture and State control of
strategic sectors, especially energy. He also spoke out for policies of
austerity, honesty, secularism and national sovereignty.

Thus the **PRD was born in 1989**. He was again a presidential candidate in
1994 and 2000, and in 1997 he became the first elected head of government of
the capital.

## Meeting With the EZLN

On May 17, 1994, Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas visited the EZLN in Guadalupe Tepeyac,
Chiapas, while he was the PRD candidate for the presidency of the republic.

Marcos received Cárdenas as a valid political interlocutor, but used his
speech to harshly criticize the PRD, which he accused of repeating the vices
of the old political class.

"Many forces support the candidacy of Mr. Cárdenas Solórzano for the
presidency of Mexico, but these will not be the decisive ones for the
transition to democracy; neither will we, the Zapatistas, be the force through
which democratizing change is reached," Marcos said.

![Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas meets Subcomandante Marcos,
1994](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/05-cardenas-
marcos-ezln-1994.jpg)Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas on the campaign trail and Marcos,
1994. Photo: La Jornada

## First Head of Government of the Federal District

The electoral victory of Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Solórzano on July 6, 1997, marked
a milestone in the struggle for the democratization of the country, as he
became **the first elected Head of Government of the then Federal District**.

The arrival of the left to lead the capital, driven by the Party of the
Democratic Revolution (PRD), meant a resounding defeat for the PRI regime and
wrested from the federal Executive control of a city that for decades suffered
the imposition of regents, thus restoring the political rights and sovereignty
of the capital's citizens.

![Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas celebrates his 1997 victory with his wife and
son](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/06-cardenas-
victory-1997.jpg)The day of the victory that made the Engineer head of
government of the Federal District, July 1997. With him are his wife and his
son Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Batel. Photo: José Antonio López / La Jornada

As Head of Government, Engineer Cárdenas inaugurated an administration with a
deep social emphasis and laid the institutional foundations for the capital's
political autonomy. His administration prioritized attention to the demands of
the popular classes, administrative transparency and the development of urban
infrastructure with an equitable vision.

Before his third presidential candidacy, in 1999, he consolidated the Federal
District as the main bastion of progressive causes in the country.

## Alongside López Obrador in the 2000 Election

As part of the transformation of the country, the Engineer fought for the
democratic transition, and in 2000 he accompanied Andrés Manuel López Obrador
in the Alliance for Mexico City, for head of government of the Federal
District.

> It is we, those of us who are here, who have provoked it, we have provoked
> it, we have undermined the regime.
>
> Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas, Zócalo rally with Andrés Manuel López Obrador, May 6,
> 2000

"We have undermined the PRI, we who are in this plaza and the millions of
Mexicans who are fighting for democracy," he added before hundreds of
Mexicans.

![Andrés Manuel López Obrador and Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas at a rally in the
Zócalo, 2000](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/04-cardenas-lopez-obrador-2000.jpg)Andrés Manuel López
Obrador and Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas at a rally in the Zócalo to support López
Obrador's candidacy, PRD, May 5, 2000. Photo: José Núñez / La Jornada

In October 2010, Cárdenas Solórzano called for the unity of the progressive
and democratic forces that "today are dispersed, divided, even confronted," as
the only ones capable of getting the country back on course. Time is short and
the pace must be quickened, he said on the 40th anniversary of the death of
his father, General Lázaro Cárdenas del Río.

The National Polytechnic Institute (IPN) awarded Engineer Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas
Solórzano an Honorary Doctorate last January for his outstanding career, his
contributions to Mexican society and his invaluable contribution to the
consolidation of democracy in the country.

During the UNAM tribute for his 90th birthday, Engineer Cárdenas recalled that
starting in 1988 the democratic struggle cost between **600 and 800** "dead,
fallen on different days. Crimes, I would say, all of them, that remain in
impunity and that have remained in impunity."

In March 2026, Petróleos Mexicanos (Pemex) announced that the company would
have an advisory commission headed by Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Solórzano.
